comparison: Perfect agreement on behavioral characterization (C1-C29). Both evaluations find the behavioral data compelling and well-supported, with OpenEval highlighting quantitative measurements and high-speed video recordings, while peer reviewers describe it as 'compelling data' without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on CR neuron characterization (C30-C40). OpenEval finds anatomical and functional data supported despite small sample sizes for calcium imaging. Peer reviewers explicitly note 'morphological and physiological identification' as compelling. OpenEval R2 also addresses C76-C78 (comparative morphology), which peer R2 includes, showing alignment on evolutionary context.

Agreement on PKD gene expression and phylogenetic analysis (C41-C44). OpenEval finds multiple complementary approaches support these claims. Peer R3 addresses broader genetic demonstration including C41-C44 plus mutant phenotypes (C45-C46, C48, C79-C84), all evaluated as supported.

Agreement on PKD mutant phenotypes (C45-C46, C48). OpenEval finds loss-of-function data well-supported with multiple alleles and batches. Peer reviewers describe 'genetic demonstration of necessity' as compelling, grouping these claims with gene expression data (C41-C44) and comparative context (C79-C84).

Perfect agreement on predation experiments (C49-C51). Both evaluations find the ecological validation supported. OpenEval notes appropriate statistical testing and controls, while peer reviewers describe 'behavioral/genetic analysis of relevance for avoiding predators' as compelling.

Divergence on connectomic reconstruction (C52-C75). OpenEval finds comprehensive circuit analysis well-supported with appropriate methodology. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the circuit is 'elegant' but noting it 'depends on EM reconstruction' and requesting additional functional validation experiments and primary EM data figures.

Agreement on comparative morphology (C76-C78). OpenEval finds comparative context well-documented through citations. Peer reviewers include these claims in their evaluation of CR neuron characterization, accepting them as part of the compelling morphological identification.

Agreement on normal CR morphology in mutants and comparative context (C79-C84). OpenEval finds SEM analysis directly supports C79 and provides appropriate comparative context. Peer reviewers group these with genetic demonstration claims, evaluating all as supported.

Agreement on uncertainty of circuit mechanisms (C89-C93). Both evaluations rate these mechanistic proposals as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes proposals are reasonable but require experimental validation. Peer reviewers describe these as 'plausible models' requiring functional testing through ablation, inactivation, or recording experiments.

Agreement on uncertainty of Rope neuron function (C94-C102). Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval finds anatomical connectivity consistent with command neuron function but requiring functional validation. Peer reviewers group with other circuit mechanisms as 'plausible models' needing experimental support.

Agreement on uncertainty of bilateral coordination mechanisms (C104-C112). Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes bilateral symmetry is well-documented but proposed mechanisms require functional testing. Peer reviewers include these in 'plausible models' that need validation through suggested experiments.

Partial overlap on discussion and future directions (C113-C117). OpenEval finds these claims appropriately acknowledge limitations and outline future directions (SUPPORTED). Peer R7 addresses broader discussion issues including C113-C117 plus background claims (C118-C134) and C103, rating as UNCERTAIN due to incomplete comparative discussion, specifically lacking C. elegans escape circuit discussion.

Divergence on background and comparative discussion (C118-C134). OpenEval finds background claims appropriately represent established literature (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, identifying 'significant lapse' in Discussion for not addressing C. elegans escape circuits, though not challenging the comparisons that are made.
